solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Possible Venetian spy, a source of misunderstanding?

parts.note: a Venetian is one kind of window blind, so a blind is a possible Venetian
to spy something is to spot it

explanation.surface: An undercover agent in Venice causes a diplomatic mix-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venetian' looks like a citizen of Venice, but here it is the slatted window covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in one's awareness or understanding, where a person fails to see something obvious, is called this.

clue.text: Guide who leads from summit currently descending on lake

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top
currently means now, at present
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A mountain leader comes down from the peak and heads onto the lake below.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'descending on' places each piece above the next. The Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult leader of a Brownie pack, the junior Girl Guides, is traditionally given this title.

clue.text: No reason for cold-callers to ring up? A winning point!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: PPI, payment protection insurance, was the subject of countless British nuisance sales and claims phone calls

explanation.surface: If you have no mis-sold insurance, the pushy phone salesmen have no excuse to call: a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole pair in this down entry. PPI was a mis-sold British loan insurance whose refund claims prompted a flood of unsolicited phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo, a full point awarded for a decisive throw or hold, which ends the bout outright, has this name.

clue.text: Was not as one desired, sadly, claiming silver

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the anagram wraps around the silver
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of desired are put in a different order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone did not get what they wanted and lost out on the gold, taking silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' is the anagram signal and 'claiming' sets the metal inside the result. 'Was not as one' reads as part of the surface, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: People who differ in opinion are not of one mind, so they are not united as one.

clue.text: Something spicy people into holy books turned up

indicators.note: into places the people inside the outer letters

parts.note: pi is crossword shorthand for pious, holy

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books
men means people

explanation.surface: Something hot and spicy gets stuffed into scripture and turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses only the books, and 'into' places the people between the holy letters and the reversed books.
explanation.definitionFit: This red pepper, often used to stuff olives, is a sweet but flavourful ingredient.

clue.text: Call from opponent in the box, ending in penalty

indicators.note: in puts the opponent inside the box

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, TV
someone who is anti something opposes it

indicators.note: ending in takes the final letter of penalty

explanation.surface: A footballer appeals after a foul by a defender in the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'ending in' are the two indicators. In the surface 'the box' is football's penalty area; in the wordplay it is the television.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old hunting cry, a shout to urge horses and hounds on at full gallop.

clue.text: Henry's left fichus arranged in a mysterious order

indicators.note: arranged means the remaining letters are put in a new order
Henry has left, so H is taken out of fichus

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away the shawls that Henry left behind, in some mysterious arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes H from FICHUS, leaving FICUS, and 'arranged' reshuffles those five letters. A fichu is a small triangular shawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufism is a mystical branch of Islam, so the adjective describes belonging to a mystic religious order.

clue.text: Boy or girl, upset seeing that, given tea

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: as means because, seeing that
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A child is upset, so someone hands over a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AS into SA, and 'given' simply adds CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: This first name is used for both sexes, so it can name a boy or a girl.

clue.text: Padding about quietly in tanktop?

parts.note: filler is material used to pad something out
ca, short for circa, means about
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone moves silently around in a sleeveless knitted pullover with padding.
explanation.walkthrough: A tank top is normally a sleeveless jumper; here it is read as the top of a fuel tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The cap closing the opening of a fuel tank sits at its top, hence a whimsical 'tanktop'.

clue.text: Secret member's call to turn over a new leaf?

parts.note: to call out is to cry

parts.words: to turn over a new leaf
parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to go on to the next page or leaf

explanation.surface: A covert party member urges others to reform their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn over a new leaf' looks like reforming one's ways, but a leaf here is a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who secretly belongs to or supports a party or group is called by this word.

clue.text: Work sailor's put together for mates

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
PO is a petty officer, a sailor, with the s of the possessive added

explanation.surface: A sailor's job has been assembled for his shipmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal, originally naval, slang for a friend or colleague, short for opposite number.

clue.text: He whom I dub X's successor, without reason

parts.note: the man I call: a he whom I give a name to
Y follows X in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A monarch names someone as heir to a ruler called X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dub' suggests knighting or crowning, but here it just means name or call.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a wild, frenzied way, as if mad, is acting without sanity or reason.

clue.text: Figure it's high time to arrest Harry!

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so noon holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: noon is the hour when the sun is highest
to harry someone is to nag them

explanation.surface: A sheriff decides the moment has come to arrest a man called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane figure with nine sides and nine angles is named from the Latin for ninth.

clue.text: Most cuckoo chicks found here?

definitions.meaning: cuckoo means silly, so the most cuckoo is the silliest
read as three words, the place where baby birds are found: within a bird's home

explanation.surface: Where would the cuckoo's chicks be found?
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo chicks famously turn up in other birds' homes, but 'cuckoo' belongs to the first sense, meaning daft.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning silly or pointless, it fits most cuckoo; split up it gives a bird's home.

clue.text: Coldplay events with alterations to 4 lyrics

indicators.note: alterations to means the letters are changed around

parts.note: the answer to 4 Down is the spicy pepper

explanation.surface: The band Coldplay rework the lyrics to their fourth song for live shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alterations to' shuffles the 4 Down answer with LYRICS. 'Coldplay' is the rock band in the surface, but means sport on snow and ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Games held every four years for skiing, skating and other snow and ice sports are play in the cold.

clue.text: Stage direction one is barking so very loudly

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loudly

explanation.surface: A dog barks so loudly that it disrupts the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' rearranges ONE IS into NOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: This direction in a script calls for sounds made offstage, such as crashes, out of the audience's view.

clue.text: Seeing what's coming forward, fellow has nervous reaction

parts.note: a prop is a forward in rugby, in the front row of the scrum
he, a male, refers to a fellow
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a nervous reaction

explanation.surface: A man sees something heading his way and flinches nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a direction but is a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to foretell events, as a seer does, is foreseeing the future.

clue.text: Aussies missing flight holding flag up, having retained title

indicators.note: holding means the birds contain the other piece

parts.note: emus are flightless Australian birds

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: Australians who missed their plane wave a flag but keep their championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the verb for flag, giving ERIT, and 'holding' wraps the birds around it. 'missing flight' looks like a delayed traveller, but describes flightless birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired professor keeps the honorary rank, so this word describes someone keeping their title after leaving.

clue.text: Merry old maiden and two Brits which I heard at promenade concert?

definitions.text: which I heard at promenade concert?

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, merry
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: two means the Brit appears twice in a row

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a Brit

explanation.surface: A tipsy young woman and two Englishmen enjoy a summer concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the old music-hall song 'I Do Like to Be Beside the Seaside', where the brass band plays on the prom (seaside promenade).
explanation.definitionFit: The song's line has the brass band playing this refrain along the seaside walk, so it is what a listener hears there.

clue.text: Always recalled George VI perhaps with stammer delivering speech

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old word meaning always
a stammer repeats the opening sound, here the first letter of the monarch
George VI is an example of a king

explanation.surface: King George VI, famous for his stammer, gives a speech, as in the film The King's Speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns AY into YA; the stammer doubles the K at the start of KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking incessantly and idly is chattering, an informal word for a flow of speech.

clue.text: Top post: one's destiny?

parts.note: post and mail both mean letters delivered
one's lot is one's fate in life

explanation.surface: Is a senior job one's destiny?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top post' reads as a senior job, but 'Top' alone is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word is a jersey worn by cyclists, as in the Tour de France's yellow jersey, or a swimsuit.

clue.text: Bank's exercises in deception

definitions.meaning: read as the plural banks: steep cliffs or headlands
pretending to hold strength one lacks, as at poker

explanation.definitionFit: Steep river banks or cliffs share their name with acts of feigned confidence meant to mislead.

clue.text: Respond in kind to storyteller in lounge?

definitions.meaning: a storyteller is a liar, so reply to one with a fib

explanation.surface: Someone answers a teller of tales while relaxing in the sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline comfortably is to relax, while answering a fibber in kind is to fib in return.

clue.text: Bloody channel volunteers to put rock music on!

indicators.note: in a down entry on means placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: AOR is album-oriented rock, a radio format
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Army reservists play rock music on a gory TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' is literal: it carries blood, and is not a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery carrying blood from the heart is a conduit for blood.

clue.text: More robust following hip and chest expander?

indicators.note: following puts the more robust piece after the other

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
haler is the comparative of hale, healthy

explanation.surface: A fitter person follows hip exercises with a chest-expanding workout device.
explanation.walkthrough: A chest expander is gym equipment; here it is a device that opens the airways.
explanation.definitionFit: This device delivers medicine to the lungs and is used to ease breathing, so it opens up the chest.

clue.text: Where waiters are passing under bar?

definitions.meaning: a state of waiting in uncertainty
the Caribbean dance of bending backwards under a pole

explanation.surface: Where do the restaurant staff go to sneak beneath the counter?
explanation.definitionFit: A state of uncertain waiting shares its name with a dance in which dancers lean back beneath a lowered pole.

clue.text: For recital, the best philosopher's works

indicators.note: for recital means as spoken out, so a word is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: the flower of something is its finest part
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher

explanation.surface: Reading out the finest works of a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like books, but it means a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory where grain is ground into baking ingredients is a works in the industrial sense.

clue.text: Egg on the faces of the elite — most pundits, too

indicators.note: the face of each word is its front, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: The upper class and most commentators end up with egg on their faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on the faces' suggests embarrassment, but 'Egg on' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or entice them to do something, a synonym of lure.

clue.text: Auditor's to instil panic in the City

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what follows is how it would sound

parts.note: to sow fear is to spread panic

explanation.surface: An auditor's job is to terrify the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant and 'the City' like London's finance district. In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria's capital is a city.

clue.text: Fume, penning article for Express

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the article goes inside

parts.note: to fume is to get cross
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A reporter is furious about writing an article for the Express newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the British newspaper but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To communicate an idea successfully is to convey or put it over to others.
